name: 14. Frontend Production Engineering and Industry Capstone

quiz.question: Why must private API keys and database secrets never be placed in Vite variables prefixed with VITE_?
options: Vite ignores variables starting with VITE_
VITE_ variables are embedded into client-side JavaScript bundles and can be inspected by any browser user
VITE_ variables only work in CSS files
They disable tree shaking
quiz.explanation: In Vite, variables prefixed with `VITE_` are exposed to browser-delivered bundles; private secrets must stay on the backend or protected server environment.

quiz.question: How do ESLint and Prettier differ in a frontend code-quality workflow?
options: Prettier compiles TypeScript, while ESLint deploys to Vercel
ESLint identifies code-quality issues and bugs, while Prettier enforces consistent code formatting
ESLint only formats CSS, while Prettier runs unit tests
They perform the exact same task
quiz.explanation: Prettier handles presentation and formatting (indentation, spacing, quotes), whereas ESLint analyzes code for potential bugs, hook rules, and unused declarations.

quiz.question: Why does an SPA hosted on Cloudflare Pages or Vercel require fallback/rewrite routing for nested URLs?
options: To disable HTTPS certificates
So direct browser navigation or refresh on nested client routes serves the SPA entry point instead of a server 404
To prevent JavaScript from loading
To bypass CORS
quiz.explanation: Without an SPA fallback rewrite to `index.html`, directly opening `/courses/frontend/react` makes the static host look for a physical file and return 404.

quiz.question: Which caching strategy is best suited for content-hashed JavaScript and CSS bundles (e.g., app.a83f21.js)?
options: no-store on every request
Long-lived immutable caching
Disabling CDN edge caching
Serving only from LocalStorage
quiz.explanation: Because content hashes change whenever file contents change, hashed assets can safely use long-lived immutable caching while HTML entries revalidate.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
options: Continuous Delivery prepares validated releases for manual approval; Continuous Deployment releases validated changes to production automatically
Continuous Deployment skips all automated tests
Continuous Delivery does not use Git
There is no difference
quiz.explanation: Continuous Delivery keeps every validated build ready to release with an approval gate, while Continuous Deployment pushes passing builds to production automatically.

quiz.question: In Service Worker caching strategies, how does Stale-While-Revalidate work?
options: It blocks all network requests permanently
It returns cached content immediately while requesting an updated version in the background
It deletes the cache before every fetch
It only works over plain HTTP
quiz.explanation: Stale-While-Revalidate serves the cached response immediately for speed while fetching a fresh copy in the background to update the cache.

quiz.question: When is Micro-Frontend architecture typically justified over a modular monolithic frontend?
options: For every small 5-page React project
When large independent teams need separate ownership and deployment lifecycles for distinct frontend domains
To remove the need for shared design tokens
To avoid writing TypeScript
quiz.explanation: Micro-frontends add operational and dependency complexity; they are justified mainly when large, independent teams need autonomous release cycles.

quiz.question: Which browser APIs support locale-aware date and number/currency formatting in internationalization (i18n)?
options: localStorage and sessionStorage
Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat
XMLHttpRequest and FormData
PerformanceObserver and IntersectionObserver
quiz.explanation: The standard `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Intl.NumberFormat` browser APIs format dates, numbers, and currencies according to user locale.

quiz.question: What is an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) used for in large frontend teams?
options: Storing database passwords in Git
Documenting the problem, options considered, chosen solution, rationale, and consequences of key technical decisions
Replacing ESLint and Prettier
Generating CSS grid layouts
quiz.explanation: ADRs preserve the context and trade-offs behind important architectural choices so growing teams understand why decisions were made.

quiz.question: What is the safest workflow before refactoring an area with high technical debt?
options: Rewrite the entire application from scratch without tests
Verify existing behavior with tests, refactor a small scoped area, re-run tests, and verify behavior
Delete package-lock.json
Disable TypeScript and linting
quiz.explanation: Safe refactoring improves internal structure without changing external behavior by establishing tests first and refactoring incrementally.
